h04.

**No — `store/db/db.go:22` is the only construction site of `mysql.NewDB` anywhere in the repository, and `store/db/db.go:8` is the only file that imports `github.com/usememos/memos/store/db/mysql`.**

Evidence:

The factory is `NewDBDriver` in `store/db/db.go`, which switches on `profile.Driver` and calls the per-driver constructor:

```18:27:store/db/db.go
	switch profile.Driver {
	case "sqlite":
		driver, err = sqlite.NewDB(profile)
	case "mysql":
		driver, err = mysql.NewDB(profile)
	case "postgres":
		driver, err = postgres.NewDB(profile)
	default:
		return nil, errors.New("unknown db driver")
	}
```

Searching all Go files for imports of `github.com/usememos/memos/store/db/...` returns only five import lines: `store/db/db.go:8-10` (the factory importing all three drivers), and `store/demo_seed_test.go:13` plus `store/deployment_config_test.go:19`, which import `store/db/sqlite` — not MySQL. A search for `mysql.NewDB` across the tree matches only `store/db/db.go:22`. Everything else that needs a driver goes through the factory: `cmd/memos/main.go:57`, `store/test/store.go:28` and `:50`, and `server/router/api/v1/test/memo_service_benchmark_test.go:70`.

One near-miss worth ruling out: `store/test/containers.go` contains several `mysql.` references (lines 42 and 101-105) and a `mysqldriver` reference, but its import block shows those are `github.com/testcontainers/testcontainers-go/modules/mysql` (spinning up a MySQL container for integration tests) and `github.com/go-sql-driver/mysql` (the upstream SQL driver used to verify connectivity), not the repo's own `store/db/mysql` package.

So the asymmetry is that SQLite is bypassed directly in two store tests, while MySQL and Postgres are reachable only through `NewDBDriver`.
